docs.title: CRISPREvo user guide
docs.text: CRISPREvo helps you prepare CRISPR data, compare spacer arrays, infer strain relationships, search candidate spacer targets and make integrated tree–array figures. Start from the material you already have; you do not need to run every tool.

docs.title: Workflow overview
docs.text: View the workflow at full size.

docs.title: Choose a tool
docs.text:
What you want to do Tool guide What to provide What you get Retrieve sequence records SeqFetcher NCBI sequence/assembly accessions or sequence UIDs FASTA and source metadata Detect arrays or filter detector results CRISPRPrep Genome FASTA, NCBI nucleotide/assembly IDs or CRISPRCasFinder JSON Processed spacer CSV and filtering report Infer relationships among strains CRISPRPhylo Processed spacer CSV for multiple strains Strain tree, optional array-tree ZIP and images Compare spacer order and sharing SpacerMap Numbered arrays or spacer sequence data Array figure, numbered arrays and cluster network Display arrays beside a tree ArrayPhyloViz Newick plus numbered arrays or SpacerMap SVG Annotated figure and editable project Find candidate sequence targets SpacerTarget Original spacer sequences with sample identities Match table, strain–target network and search report

Each guide explains input preparation, exact page controls, parameter choices, result interpretation, downloads and common problems. Button names follow the current interface: CRISPRPrep uses Run, SpacerTarget uses Search, and the other tools use Commit (the CRISPRPhylo control may read Build tree after a run).

docs.title: First visit
docs.text: Follow the quick start for a small, reproducible plotting example, then the end-to-end workflow for real multi-strain data. The input reference explains which file belongs in which tool; downloads explains what to keep.

docs.title: Before interpreting an analysis
docs.text:
Check sample identities, retained data and the settings applied to the result. Shared spacer IDs describe the chosen numbering scheme; a tree describes the selected inference; a target match describes sequence similarity under the selected search and filters. The tool guides explain these distinctions with examples.

Save Copy results link once a Job ID appears. Accepted analyses continue on the server after closing the tab, and My Jobs restores results from all six tools. Results expire seven days after the task ends; download important outputs and retain original inputs/settings. In ArrayPhyloViz, save a new private snapshot or project JSON after further edits. See troubleshooting for recovery help.

docs.title: Citing CRISPREvo
docs.text:
A formal CRISPREvo manuscript citation is not yet provided here. Use the source repository and the exact software version for attribution until a preferred citation becomes available.

Until then, cite the CRISPREvo source repository and record the exact release tag or Git commit used:

CRISPREvo: CRISPR evolutionary analysis web platform. Source code: https://github.com/zwxyo/crisprevo

docs.title: Underlying tools and services
docs.text:
Cite the methods used in your run as appropriate:

  • CRISPRCasFinder for CRISPR detection.
  • NCBI records, E-utilities and NCBI Datasets for retrieved sequences and assemblies.
  • NCBI BLAST and target accessions for SpacerTarget searches; retain search date, database, hit limit, filters and the report.
  • The GraphMSA or CRISPRFormer method used for tree inference, once the project-specific preferred citations are supplied.

The documentation structure and task-oriented style were informed by the CRISPR Comparison Toolkit documentation, particularly its separation of quick usage, tutorials, input contracts, and tool-specific pages. CRISPREvo behavior described here is based on the current CRISPREvo web implementation.

docs.title: Information to record
docs.text: For reproducibility, report the CRISPREvo release/commit, access date, input source, processing settings, SpacerMap alignment and clustering, color seed, tree method, repeat-distance setting, CRISPRFormer profile where applicable, any chosen root, and manual edits made in ArrayPhyloViz. Keep original inputs, settings and downloaded outputs separately: private results links expire after seven days, and saved reports do not retain every submitted parameter.

docs.title: My Jobs: save, retrieve and download results
docs.text: Use My Jobs (/my-jobs) to return to work from all six tools without an account. Each submitted analysis receives a full Job ID and private results link. Keep that link: the browser history is a convenience, not the result archive.

docs.title: Save access when submitting
docs.text:
1. Submit the input in the tool and wait until a Job ID and private link appear. Do not close the page while it is still uploading or submitting.
  2. Select Copy results link and save it with your sample notes.
  3. Once the job is accepted, you can close the page. Server processing continues.
  4. Open the saved link later, or use My Jobs → Retrieve a job to paste the full ID or link and select Retrieve.

Individual tool pages also offer Retrieve previous results. If an ID belongs to another tool, the shared retrieval control directs you to that job's results page. Use the full 32-character ID, not a shortened display fragment.

In ArrayPhyloViz, Commit composes the figure and attempts to save an initial project snapshot. After further edits, select Save private link again to create a new snapshot with a new ID. An older link does not automatically acquire later edits. Save project downloads JSON for local reopening and long-term storage.

docs.title: Understand status before interpreting a result
docs.text:
Status Meaning and action Queued Accepted and waiting to start. Keep the link; do not repeatedly submit the same input. Waiting for resources Accepted, but server capacity is temporarily insufficient. Wait for the existing job; queue position may be shown. Running Processing is in progress. Read the current phase; an activity bar is not a reliable completion-time estimate. Finished Processing ended successfully. Open the results and check their actual content; an empty biological result can still be a successful run. Partially finished Some inputs or steps failed while others produced output. Review the failed IDs/batches before interpreting coverage of the dataset. Failed / Cancelled Processing stopped. Available partial output can still be downloaded; a new analysis requires resubmitting input. Unavailable The job could not be retrieved. Check the full link, service availability and expiry.

A busy-service error before a Job ID appears means the submission was not accepted. Wait for the displayed retry interval, then submit again. This differs from an accepted job waiting in the queue.

docs.title: Browse the history
docs.text:
Filter by Tool, Status or job name/ID. Select the Submitted heading to switch newest/oldest first, and use Previous / Next for the six-row pages. Times are shown in your local time zone. Refresh checks current status.

Action What it does View Opens the job's results page. Copy link Copies the private results link. Download Downloads the saved result report when available; this is not every tool-specific export. Review results Opens a failed, partial or cancelled job to inspect available evidence. Remove Removes the reference from browser history only. It neither cancels nor deletes the server job. Export job links Downloads all links in this browser history, including entries hidden by filters. It does not download result data.

On the results page, use Open results to restore the interactive tool and access its exports. The page also offers Download result report and a primary output where supported: processed CSV, FASTA, Newick, SpacerMap SVG or project JSON. For CRISPRPhylo array-tree ZIP, reopen the interactive tool.

docs.title: Use another device
docs.text:
History is kept for the current browser tab by default. Enable Remember job history on this device to keep references across visits on that device. Turning it off removes the persistent history copy, not the server results.

History does not synchronize automatically. Open a saved link on the other device, or copy lines from Export job links into Retrieve a job. Up to 100 links/IDs can be imported at once. Anyone with a private link can access the job, so share links only with intended collaborators.

docs.title: Retention and reproducibility
docs.text:
Results and job records expire seven days after the task ends, including partial, failed and cancelled tasks. The results page displays an expiry time when available. Input workspaces are deleted at task completion; retrieving a result does not restore every original upload, parameter or run log.

Keep original inputs and a separate record of settings. CRISPRPrep results retain CSVs, counts, warnings and generated detection JSON when applicable, but uploaded JSON and processing options are not part of its saved result. CRISPRPhylo retains the original inferred tree and method fields, but not the input CSV or run log. SpacerTarget retains match evidence and query IDs; original full query sequences and search parameters are removed from terminal job reports. Other outputs, such as fetched FASTA and saved figure projects, remain downloadable until expiry.

Download important files before expiry. Neither Remember job history, Export job links, nor opening a link extends retention. For a failed or cancelled analysis, submit your input again. SeqFetcher's Retry failed and Resume pending submit selected sets of IDs as new jobs; they do not modify the previous job. SpacerTarget has no in-place retry after completion.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This walkthrough uses small illustrative data so you can learn what the plots mean before processing a real dataset. The example Newick is supplied for practice; it is not a tree inferred from the numbered arrays.

docs.title: 1. Plot three arrays
docs.text:
Download example-arrays.txt, or paste:

strain_A    1,2,3,6,7,9
strain_B    1,2,4,6,8,9
strain_C    10,2,4,6,8
  1. Open SpacerMap from Analysis.
  2. Paste the text or upload the file, using only one input method.
  3. Keep Right alignment and No clustering.
  4. Select Commit.

You should see three rows, 9 distinct spacer labels and 6 shared labels. There are 17 spacer occurrences in total. IDs 3 and 7 occur only in strain A; ID 10 occurs only in strain C. Those array-specific types are triangles. Shared types connect across neighboring rows where applicable.

Try Ancestral spacer and commit again: A and B share the rightmost ID 9, while C ends in 8 and forms its own group. Then try Shared spacer: all three arrays connect because every pair shares at least two distinct IDs. Show cluster network displays those links. This illustrates that different grouping rules answer different questions.

Choose SVG and Download SVG. Download numbered file is unnecessary for already numbered input; retain the example TXT.

docs.title: 2. Combine the arrays with a tree
docs.text:
Download example-tree.nwk, or copy:

((strain_A:0.12,strain_B:0.08)95:0.05,strain_C:0.18);
  1. Open ArrayPhyloViz.
  2. Add the tree under Phylogenetic tree.
  3. Add the same arrays under CRISPR arrays, using the TXT or your exported SpacerMap SVG.
  4. Select Exact names, then Commit.
  5. Open Review and edit mapping: all three arrays should map to three leaves, with none unassigned.
  6. Adjust row spacing and label space. Turn on Use branch lengths to compare proportional lengths with the default topology layout.
  7. Keep the private link created by Commit. After edits, use Save private link again or Save project for a local JSON, then export SVG, PNG or PDF.

The tree groups A and B together. The array track helps inspect which types they share with each other and C. The internal label 95 came from the example tree; the editor did not calculate support. Reopen the saved JSON with Open saved project to continue editing.

docs.title: 3. Try data preparation and inference
docs.text:
For a detector-free trial, open CRISPRPrep → Import JSON results → Load example JSON, keep the defaults and select Run. Examine retained/filtered arrays and the processed-row preview, then download Processed CSV and the report. To compare a different filter, load the example JSON again, change that filter and select Run for a new job. Keep a record of the settings for each result.

To try tree inference, open CRISPRPhylo → Load example, keep GraphMSA, then select Commit. This requires the site's inference service and can take time. Inspect the Newick source and download .nwk. Leave Repeat grouping distance at 0 for this first trial. Enable Also build array trees before submission if you also want the group-level ZIP. The built-in examples in different tools are independent; they are not automatically a matched dataset.

docs.title: 4. Try sequence retrieval or target searching
docs.text:
SeqFetcher → Load example → Commit retrieves example nucleotide records from NCBI. Check metadata, keep the private results link, and download FASTA/ZIP for your records. For a whole-genome assembly, enter its GCA_/GCF_ accession with Nucleotide selected; one retrieved row may contain multiple FASTA contigs. These examples demonstrate retrieval, not bacterial CRISPR detection.

For SpacerTarget, use Load example or example-spacers.fasta, review the settings, then select Search. This submits a real NCBI search. Save Copy results link. Results depend on the database and search time, so no fixed hit count is expected. Follow the SpacerTarget guide to interpret Strict/Exact filters and network edges.

After a job is accepted, test recovery by copying its link into My Jobs → Retrieve a job. Open the result and confirm it is the expected dataset. Downloads and original inputs are still needed for long-term storage because server results expire after seven days.

Continue with the real-data workflow once input names and result types are familiar.

docs.title: The detector is unavailable
docs.text: Sequence detection requires the configured CRISPRCasFinder service to be available. Select Refresh status. If it remains unavailable, import a result.json generated elsewhere or ask the administrator to configure the detector command and working directory.

docs.title: A detection job disappeared
docs.text: Use My Jobs → Retrieve a job or Retrieve previous results and paste the full ID/private link. Default browser history is tab-local, but the accepted job remains on the server. Results expire seven days after the task ends; after expiry, submit your saved input again. See My Jobs for recovery and retention.

docs.title: JSON produced no spacer rows
docs.text: Check the evidence threshold, minimum spacer count, orientation fields, and N filter. Direct JSON import in SpacerMap applies fixed evidence 3/4 and ND/N rules; use CRISPRPrep for adjustable filtering and a detailed report.

docs.title: SpacerMap rejected the input
docs.text: Use one input method at a time. Numbered text must follow array_name<TAB>spacer1,spacer2,…. A direction-folder upload must contain FASTA files beneath a folder whose name includes pos/forward or neg/reverse.

docs.title: SpacerMap colors changed
docs.text: Keep the color seed unchanged and rerender. Archive the numbered spacer file because it fixes the relationship between spacer sequences and displayed IDs.

docs.title: CRISPRPhylo rejected the CSV
docs.text: Confirm that the CSV contains the complete required header, at least two distinct nonempty Folder values, and at least two usable spacer rows. Negative arrays need a value in Reverse_Complement_Sequence.

docs.title: The tree pipeline timed out or is missing
docs.text: The web adapter stops a CRISPRPhylo run after 15 minutes. Reduce the dataset or run the underlying research pipeline outside the website. A missing script, model, or output-tree error requires administrator action on the server.

docs.title: Arrays did not match tree leaves
docs.text: ArrayPhyloViz matches original Newick leaf IDs rather than display labels or row order. Review exact spelling first, then try suffix removal or case/outer-space normalization. Ambiguous normalized names are deliberately left unmatched.

docs.title: An exported SVG cannot be reopened
docs.text: Only SVG files exported by the current SpacerMap/ArrayPhyloViz version contain supported editable metadata. For older images, reopen the numbered array text and Newick source, or use a saved ArrayPhyloViz project JSON.

docs.title: A PNG export failed
docs.text: Large composed figures are limited to 32 million pixels. Reduce the PNG scale or export SVG.

docs.title: Browser results disappeared after refresh
docs.text: Retrieve the saved private link to reopen server results. Unsaved ArrayPhyloViz edits and CRISPRPhylo root changes are local: save a project/snapshot or rerooted Newick before leaving. A result link restores the saved version only. Keeping browser history does not extend the seven-day server retention.

docs.title: SpacerTarget shows no matches
docs.text: Check whether all query batches completed. A partial/failed job is not evidence of no targets. Clear table filters, inspect All candidates TSV, and use Explore to inspect lower-coverage or lower-identity alignments. No returned matches refers only to the selected database, hit limit and search configuration.

docs.title: SpacerTarget table and network counts differ
docs.text: Rows are occurrence–site matches; edge weight counts different supporting sequences. Unassigned strains are omitted from the graph and only 200 nodes are displayed. Network type checkboxes can hide nodes without changing table/export filters. Use the filtered TSV to inspect all rows.

docs.title: A SpacerTarget task was interrupted
docs.text: Retrieve the full ID/link and review Details and any successful batches. Inputs are deleted at task end, so the current workflow requires resubmission of original spacers for a new search; there is no in-place Retry failed operation. Local waiting for resources and remote NCBI searching are separate stages. Use the displayed NCBI request link to inspect a submitted remote request, rather than repeatedly creating duplicate jobs.

docs.title: Fewer strains or arrays appear than expected
docs.text: In processed CSV, Folder groups strains and Seq_Name groups arrays. A single CRISPRPrep detection input is one sample even if it contains several FASTA records. Detect different strains separately, then import their JSON together. For custom SpacerMap CSV, make every distinct array's Seq_Name unique across strains.

docs.title: SeqFetcher exported records hidden by search
docs.text: Search filters the table, not the selection. The header checkbox affects visible retrieved records; hidden selected rows remain selected. Check the selection count before export. Retry failed submits all failed IDs as a new job independently of row selection; save the earlier private link to retain access to successes.

docs.title: A job is waiting for resources
docs.text: If a Job ID is present, keep the link and wait for the accepted task. If submission returned a busy response without an ID, wait for its retry interval and resubmit. The progress indicator shows activity and phases, not a guaranteed finish time.

docs.title: Assembly retrieval failed or returned several FASTA records
docs.text: Use Nucleotide for GCA_/GCF_ IDs. Several contigs under one assembly are expected; the length is their total. Check the failed-ID message for package/version/length validation and size limits. SeqFetcher uses one ID per request when assemblies are present; a single assembly exceeding the response limit still needs another workflow.

docs.title: CRISPRPrep cannot rerun with new settings after recovery
docs.text: Saved results retain outputs, not uploaded source JSON or processing options. Upload your original JSON again, or download CRISPRCasFinder JSON from a detection result and re-import it. Set the filters explicitly and select Run. A form showing default values does not prove those values were used for the retrieved result.

docs.title: CRISPRPhylo shows no run log or forgets a new root
docs.text: The saved report omits the run log and input CSV. Check the job status and tree rather than treating a blank log as failure. Rerooting is local to the current page; download the changed Newick. Restoring the job brings back the original tree. Midpoint rooting requires known nonnegative lengths with a positive tree diameter.

docs.title: The array-tree count is smaller than expected
docs.text: Enable Also build array trees before submission. Inspect ZIP index.csv: a single-array group is marked skipped_single_array and has no Newick file. Use (group_id, tree_label) in labels.csv to recover original array identities.

docs.title: Reporting a problem
docs.text: Include the tool name, browser, time of the run, selected settings, exact error message, and the smallest non-sensitive input that reproduces the issue. Do not attach confidential or unpublished sequence data to a public issue.

docs.title: End-to-end workflow
docs.text:
Start at the first step for which you have suitable data. Spacer visualization, tree inference and target searching are separate downstream uses of prepared spacers; target searching is optional and does not need a tree.

View the workflow at full size.

docs.title: 1. Retrieve or collect genome sequences
docs.text:
Use SeqFetcher for nucleotide or GCA_/GCF_ assembly accessions/UIDs, or start with your own genome FASTA. Verify accession, organism and sequence length. Save metadata and maintain a sample list linking each strain to its input records.

Keep contigs from one strain together. Do not combine unrelated strains in one detection input and expect FASTA headers to create separate strain identities. Protein records are not genome-detection inputs.

docs.title: 2. Detect each sample and prepare a combined spacer table
docs.text:
In CRISPRPrep, detect one sample per run from FASTA, or select NCBI accession to retrieve nucleotide/assembly records and detect automatically. Keep contigs of one assembly together. A list spanning several strains is combined into one detection input and does not automatically become several strain IDs. Download CRISPRCasFinder JSON from each detection run and save it under a meaningful sample name. Alternatively, use existing CRISPRCasFinder outputs arranged as sample_A/result.json, sample_B/result.json, and so on.

Import the JSON results together, set evidence/count/direction/N filters, and select Run. Review Filtered out arrays and the report before changing thresholds. Keep original JSON and download Unprocessed CSV, Processed CSV and the report. Record filtering settings separately; uploaded JSON and processing options are not retained in the saved result.

Check these identities in the processed table:

Field Downstream role Folder Strain grouping in CRISPRPhylo and SpacerTarget. All arrays belonging to one strain should share it. Seq_Name Array grouping in SpacerMap and array identity in SpacerTarget. Use a unique name for each distinct array. Organism_Name Description-derived organism label and grouping for CRISPRPrep's organism-wide N filter; it is not the strain ID.

docs.title: 3. Infer strain relationships with CRISPRPhylo
docs.text:
Transfer the processed CSV using CRISPRPrep’s CRISPRPhylo link, or paste/upload it to CRISPRPhylo. Confirm at least two usable strain IDs, select GraphMSA or CRISPRFormer and a model profile where applicable, and set Repeat grouping distance (start at 0). Read the method-specific meaning of this control in the guide. Enable Also build array trees if needed, then select Commit.

Check leaf names and Newick. Download the strain tree, optional array-tree ZIP and result report, and record method/profile and repeat distance. Use midpoint or branch rooting only with a justified interpretation. Download any changed Newick before leaving: the saved job keeps its original root. Tree relationships depend on the retained CRISPR evidence and method; vertical leaf order and completion status are not measures of evolutionary confidence.

docs.title: 4. Compare array structure with SpacerMap
docs.text:
Upload the same processed CSV to SpacerMap, start with Right / No clustering, and select Commit. Review names, order, array-specific triangles and shared IDs. Only interpret leader/trailer ends after confirming orientation from the source data.

Try Shared spacer to inspect groups connected by two or more IDs, or Ancestral spacer to group identical rightmost IDs. Export SVG and Download numbered file. Keep the numbered file to preserve the IDs used in the figure; re-numbering a different subset may assign different labels.

docs.title: 5. Search candidate targets when relevant
docs.text:
Upload the processed CSV to SpacerTarget, or select the SpacerTarget link below CRISPRPrep’s downloads. Verify that original spacer sequences are 15–100 A/C/G/T bases and that sample IDs are present. Choose the hit limit and select Search.

Save the results link. On completion, inspect Strict matches, open alignments, then compare Exact or Explore if needed. A sequence match does not establish a functional CRISPR target or infection relationship. Download all candidates, the search report and a filtered TSV documenting the evidence used in your study.

Do not substitute SpacerMap numbered TXT: a spacer number has no searchable nucleotide sequence.

docs.title: 6. Compose an integrated figure
docs.text:
Open ArrayPhyloViz, upload Newick and the SpacerMap SVG or numbered TXT, and select Commit.

Match arrays to the original leaf names. Seq_Name may differ from Folder; use the processed table to assign arrays manually when suffix matching is insufficient. Review all missing leaves and unassigned arrays. Multiple arrays can belong to one strain.

Adjust label space, row spacing, branch display and annotations. Save project JSON and mapping TSV, then export SVG, PNG or PDF. Use Save private link to preserve the current edited snapshot for recovery through My Jobs. A saved project preserves figure edits; the processed CSV and original JSON preserve their sequence basis.

docs.title: Keep an analysis bundle
docs.text:
Keep sample metadata, original FASTA/JSON, processing report, processed CSV, numbered arrays, Newick, optional target-search report/TSVs, final mapping, editable project and exported figures. Record the analysis date, software version if available, filtering choices, tree method/profile, SpacerMap grouping/alignment/seed and figure edits.

Save private results links as you proceed; My Jobs can restore accepted jobs across devices. Results expire seven days after completion and inputs are deleted at task end, so links do not replace downloaded evidence or a settings record.

See Downloads for a file-by-file guide and Troubleshooting for recovery steps.

docs.title: Documentation checklist
docs.text: Use this checklist when the web application changes.

docs.title: Before editing
docs.text:
• Identify the deployed application version or source commit.
  • Test the affected page with a minimal valid input and one invalid input.
  • Record any new input limits, defaults, file formats, buttons, and downloads.

docs.title: Update the right pages
docs.text:
• User steps and parameter meaning: the matching page under docs/tools/.
  • Cross-tool hand-off: docs/workflow.md.
  • File schema or parsing behavior: docs/reference/input-formats.md.
  • New or changed output: docs/reference/downloads.md.
  • Size, count, retention, or timeout change: docs/reference/limits.md.
  • Recoverable failure: docs/troubleshooting.md.
  • Public tool added or removed: docs/index.md and mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
1. Run python -m mkdocs build --strict.
  2. Preview the site on desktop and mobile widths.
  3. Follow every changed procedure in the deployed web app.
  4. Confirm exact UI labels, defaults, links, and downloaded filenames.
  5. Confirm that no unpublished sample IDs, sequence data, local paths, tokens, or API keys appear in the repository.
  6. Open a pull request and inspect the Read the Docs preview before merging.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
• Merge the reviewed documentation change to main.
  • Confirm the latest Read the Docs build succeeds.
  • For a software release, create/activate the matching documentation tag and verify stable.
  • Update the web application's Documentation links to the final Read the Docs URL.

docs.title: Read the Docs deployment
docs.text: The repository is configured for MkDocs Material. Read the Docs reads .readthedocs.yaml, creates a Python 3.12 environment, installs requirements.txt, and builds mkdocs.yml in strict mode.

docs.title: 1. Review project metadata
docs.text:
Before the first public build:

  1. Replace the web-application URL note in docs/index.md with the deployed CRISPREvo URL.
  2. Replace the placeholder citation in docs/citation.md when the preferred citation is available.
  3. Confirm the author, copyright year, repository links, and license.
  4. Make sure every currently public tool is represented in mkdocs.yml navigation.

docs.title: 2. Build locally
docs.text:
From the documentation repository root:

Windows PowerShellLinux or macOS 
py -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m mkdocs serve

python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m mkdocs serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ and check navigation, code blocks, tables, light/dark themes, internal links, and images. Then run:

python -m mkdocs build --strict

The generated site/ directory is local build output and should not be committed.

docs.title: 3. Commit and push to GitHub
docs.text:
git add .
git commit -m "Add CRISPREvo user documentation"
git push -u origin main

The configured repository is https://github.com/zwxyo/CRISPREvo-docs.

docs.title: 4. Import the project
docs.text:
1. Sign in at readthedocs.org with GitHub.
  2. Install or authorize the Read the Docs GitHub App for zwxyo/CRISPREvo-docs.
  3. On the Read the Docs dashboard, select Add project.
  4. Search for and select CRISPREvo-docs.
  5. Keep main as the default branch and choose a unique project name/slug such as crisprevo if available.
  6. Continue and confirm that .readthedocs.yaml exists at the repository root.
  7. Open Builds and inspect the first build log.

With GitHub App integration, pushes trigger builds automatically and no manual webhook is needed.

docs.title: 5. Verify the published site
docs.text:
Check these URLs using the slug selected during import:

https://<project-slug>.readthedocs.io/en/latest/
https://<project-slug>.readthedocs.io/en/latest/quickstart/
https://<project-slug>.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tools/spacermap/

Confirm that search works, the version selector shows latest, the workflow image loads, and Edit on GitHub points to the documentation repository.

docs.title: 6. Enable review and version workflows
docs.text:
Read the Docs enables pull-request builds by default for new GitHub-connected projects. Verify this under Settings → Pull request builds. Each documentation pull request can then receive a hosted preview before merge.

latest follows the default branch. To publish stable documentation, create semantic Git tags such as v1.0.0, activate the corresponding version in Read the Docs, and set stable as the default when appropriate.

docs.title: 7. Diagnose a failed build
docs.text:
Build stage Likely cause Fix Configuration validation Invalid .readthedocs.yaml key or indentation Compare with the Read the Docs v2 configuration reference. Dependency installation Unavailable or incompatible pinned version Test pip install -r requirements.txt in Python 3.12 and update pins deliberately. MkDocs configuration Missing page in nav, extension, or theme Run mkdocs build --strict locally. Image/link warnings File path or filename case mismatch Use paths relative to the current Markdown page and match case exactly. Repository clone GitHub App cannot access the repository Re-authorize the app or reconnect the repository in project settings.

Do not add application runtime dependencies to this repository. Read the Docs builds only the static user guide.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text:
Save the output appropriate to your next step. A private results link restores a job for seven days; it is not a permanent file archive. Tool-specific downloads are available after Open results from My Jobs.

Tool Download Contents and use SeqFetcher FASTA Selected full-length records, deduplicated by returned accession. An assembly contains multiple contigs in one FASTA. SeqFetcher Metadata TSV / ZIP Selected metadata; ZIP adds combined/per-accession FASTA, metadata JSON, run report and failed/pending ID lists. CRISPRPrep CRISPRCasFinder JSON Generated detector output, available for detection jobs. Re-import it to change filters or combine samples. Uploaded source JSON must be kept separately. CRISPRPrep Unprocessed CSV spacers_unprocessed.csv: spacer rows after evidence/count filtering, before direction/N normalization. CRISPRPrep Processed CSV spacers_processed.csv: filtered/normalized rows and reverse-complement/effective-repeat fields. Use in SpacerMap, CRISPRPhylo or SpacerTarget. CRISPRPrep Processing report Counts, warnings, array outcomes and retrieval failures where applicable. Saved processing options are omitted; record them separately. SpacerMap Numbered TXT Array names and ordered spacer IDs from sequence conversion. Preserve these for consistent reuse. SpacerMap SVG / raster image Array diagram; supported SVG carries editable array metadata. PNG/JPEG/TIFF/WEBP use the chosen DPI. CRISPRPhylo Download .nwk Current displayed tree, including local rerooting. My Jobs' direct tree download retains the original inferred root. CRISPRPhylo Download tree SVG or PNG of the complete current strain tree, independent of zoom/pan. CRISPRPhylo Download array trees (.zip) Optional group Newick files, index.csv, labels.csv and README.txt; enable before running. Not included inside the result JSON. SpacerTarget Export filtered TSV Match rows passing current table filters and node/edge focus, across all table pages. SpacerTarget All candidates TSV All returned alignments without Strict/current table filtering; not an exhaustive database search. SpacerTarget Search report Retained query/occurrence identifiers, match evidence, annotation status and batch history. Terminal reports omit original full sequences, parameters and raw BLAST responses. SpacerTarget PNG / SVG Current association network view. Preserve TSV/report as supporting evidence. ArrayPhyloViz Save project Editable local project JSON with mapping, tree, styles and figure edits. ArrayPhyloViz Save private link A server snapshot of the project with its own ID and expiry; later edits require another save. ArrayPhyloViz Mapping TSV Array-to-leaf assignments, spacer counts and displayed reversals. ArrayPhyloViz SVG / PNG / PDF Complete integrated figure. SVG embeds project data; PDF is downloaded directly and is not a replacement for the editable JSON. ArrayPhyloViz Newick Full tree in edited child order, using original names and branch lengths. Display annotations live in the project. My Jobs Export job links Plain-text links for importing history on another device; no sequence data or figures are included.

docs.title: Does a visible filter affect downloads?
docs.text:
Tool Scope SeqFetcher Selected retrieved rows, including selected rows hidden by search. The header checkbox affects only visible rows. CRISPRPrep All rows produced by the run's processing settings, regardless of preview search/page. SpacerTarget Filtered TSV follows table filters and graph focus; All candidates ignores them. Network type-visibility checkboxes affect the drawing only. SpacerMap / CRISPRPhylo Complete figure, independent of preview zoom/pan. CRISPRPhylo uses the current local root. ArrayPhyloViz Complete figure at selected export resolution; collapsed clades and styles affect the drawing.

SpacerTarget table rows count occurrence–site matches; network edge weights count different supporting query sequences. Those totals need not agree. After input cleanup, the TSV sequence column can be blank while alignment evidence remains; keep original input FASTA/CSV for complete spacer sequences.

docs.title: Minimum analysis bundle
docs.text:
Keep original accessions/FASTA/JSON, sample identities, a separate settings record, processing report, processed CSV, numbered arrays, original and any rerooted Newick, optional array-tree ZIP, figure mapping/project and final images. For target searches add original spacers, database/hit limit/filter settings, all candidates, filtered TSV and search report.

Record analysis date and software version when available, method/profile, repeat-distance value, processing thresholds, alignment/clustering, color seed and relevant figure edits. Server reports omit some input-related fields by design; do not rely on a result link alone to reproduce an analysis.

docs.title: Input formats
docs.text: Use this page to choose the correct input and preserve sample identities. Save text files as UTF-8. Examples are illustrative, not biological validation datasets.

docs.title: Which file goes where?
docs.text: File/data Tool NCBI sequence accessions or UIDs SeqFetcher; nucleotide IDs also work in CRISPRPrep’s NCBI accession mode GCA_/GCF_ assembly accession SeqFetcher in Nucleotide mode, or CRISPRPrep’s NCBI accession mode Genome/contig FASTA from one sample CRISPRPrep detection CRISPRCasFinder JSON CRISPRPrep; SpacerMap and SpacerTarget accept it with different filtering rules Processed spacer CSV SpacerMap, CRISPRPhylo, SpacerTarget Spacer FASTA SpacerMap or SpacerTarget, with different grouping conventions below Numbered arrays SpacerMap and ArrayPhyloViz; not SpacerTarget or CRISPRPhylo Newick tree plus arrays ArrayPhyloViz Saved Composer project JSON ArrayPhyloViz Open saved project

docs.title: Genome FASTA
docs.text:
Every record begins with a unique > header followed by IUPAC DNA sequence. CRISPRPrep accepts one file with multiple contigs per detection run. Treat that input as one sample; process different strains separately before batch-importing their JSON results.

>sample_A_contig_1
ATGCGTACGTTAGCTAGCTAGCTAGCTAGC
>sample_A_contig_2
GGCATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGTTA

These short sequences demonstrate syntax only; they are not expected to produce CRISPR arrays.

docs.title: NCBI ID list
docs.text: Use one or more nucleotide IDs such as NC_012920.1 or NM_000546.6, or protein IDs such as NP_000537.3 in a separate Protein run. Newlines, commas, spaces and semicolons separate IDs. Uploaded TXT/CSV/TSV must contain IDs only, with no column header. Sequence UIDs are accepted. GCA_/GCF_ assembly accessions are accepted in Nucleotide mode, for example GCF_000339015.1. They identify an assembly whose downloaded FASTA preserves separate chromosome/contig records. Gene, Taxonomy, BioProject and SRA IDs are not supported. CRISPRPrep accepts up to 100 nucleotide/assembly IDs and combines successful records into one detection input; SeqFetcher accepts up to 500 IDs. Both submitted ID lists are limited to 16,000 characters.

docs.title: CRISPRCasFinder JSON
docs.text:
Provide the detector's result object containing Sequences, each sequence's Crisprs, and each array's Regions. Keep the original JSON for reprocessing.

Import destination What happens CRISPRPrep Adjustable evidence/count filters plus optional unknown-direction and organism-wide N exclusion. Default minimum evidence is 1 and minimum spacer count is 2. SpacerMap Fixed evidence 3–4 filtering, unresolved ND removal and organism-wide N exclusion. SpacerTarget Retains all spacer regions regardless of evidence/direction; each JSON file is one sample. Every sequence must still pass its 15–100 A/C/G/T validation.

Use CRISPRPrep if filtering needs to be explicit and documented. A processing report, target-search report or figure-project JSON is not interchangeable with detector JSON. CRISPRPrep’s CRISPRCasFinder JSON download supplies generated detector output; keep any JSON you upload separately, because saved jobs do not retain those uploads.

docs.title: Processed spacer CSV
docs.text:
Each row is one spacer occurrence. CRISPRPhylo requires this complete header; CRISPRPrep output includes additional useful columns:

Folder,Seq_Name,Orientation,Spacer_Sequence,DR_Consensus,Reverse_Complement_Sequence,Reverse_Complement_DR
strain_A,strain_A_CRISPR1,+,ACGTACGT,TGCA,,
strain_A,strain_A_CRISPR1,+,GATTACAA,TGCA,,
strain_B,strain_B_CRISPR1,-,ACTTAGCA,GCAT,TGCTAAGT,ATGC
strain_B,strain_B_CRISPR1,-,GCCATGGA,GCAT,TCCATGGC,ATGC

This is a format illustration; its short spacers are not suitable SpacerTarget input. Use actual processed data for analysis. Keep rows from each array in their intended order, and retain reverse-complement columns supplied by CRISPRPrep.

Field Identity rule Folder Strain ID for CRISPRPhylo and SpacerTarget. Do not merge different strains under the same value. Seq_Name Array ID. SpacerMap groups by this field alone, so different arrays need globally unique names. Organism_Name Description-derived label, used by CRISPRPrep's organism-wide N filter; not a substitute for strain ID.

SpacerMap accepts pasted CSV as well as uploaded CSV when its header includes Spacer_Sequence. Its minimum custom CSV header is Seq_Name,Orientation,Spacer_Sequence. It can compute a missing negative-strand reverse complement. CRISPRPhylo requires all seven columns and a usable reverse-complement spacer value for reverse rows. Effective_DR in CRISPRPrep output is the orientation-appropriate repeat.

docs.title: Numbered arrays
docs.text:
Use one array per line. A tab separates the unique name from its spacer IDs; commas, spaces or semicolons separate IDs.

strain_A    1,2,3,6,7,9
strain_B    1,2,4,6,8,9
strain_C    10,2,4,6,8

Download this example. IDs identify types within the dataset, not globally across runs. Generate IDs for all arrays together in SpacerMap, then reuse the numbered TXT. DNA arrays in uploaded TXT/TSV can be converted automatically by SpacerMap; pasted array-format text treats tokens as labels; a recognized spacer CSV is converted through the CSV route.

docs.title: Spacer FASTA and direction folders
docs.text:
For SpacerMap, one uploaded FASTA represents one array, each record one spacer. Numeric record headers are used directly as IDs; other headers trigger sequence-based numbering. For multiple arrays, choose a folder such as:

dataset/
  pos/
    strain_A.fasta
    strain_B.fasta
  neg/
    strain_C.fasta

Folder names containing pos/forward or neg/reverse identify direction. Either side can be absent. Relative paths contribute to array names, so you may need manual matching to tree leaves later. Supply spacer records, not whole contigs.

For SpacerTarget, use >strain|array|spacer to encode sample identity:

>strain_A|CRISPR1|spacer_1
CGCCAGGGTTTTCCCAGTCACGACGTTGTAAA

Each sequence must be 15–100 A/C/G/T bases. Download an example. Alternatively use a header such as >spacer_1 strain=strain_A array=CRISPR1 source=NC_000000.1, replacing the placeholder source accession. Without strain metadata, matches appear in the table but not the strain network.

SpacerTarget CSV/TSV requires sequence or Spacer_Sequence. Supported metadata includes strain_id (aliases strain, Folder), strain_name, array_id (alias Seq_Name), spacer_id, orientation (alias Orientation) and source_accession. Sequence-only tables are searchable but lack strain mapping.

docs.title: Newick
docs.text:
ArrayPhyloViz accepts one Newick tree with unique leaf names and a final semicolon:

((strain_A:0.12,strain_B:0.08)95:0.05,strain_C:0.18);

Download this illustrative tree. Colon values are branch lengths; 95 is an internal label supplied by the input. Quoted labels are accepted. Bracket comments are ignored. Matching uses original leaf names, not edited display labels.

docs.title: Array-tree ZIP
docs.text: Enable Also build array trees in CRISPRPhylo before running. Each group_*.nwk contains arrays from one repeat group. index.csv lists built and skipped groups; labels.csv maps each (group_id, tree_label) to an original array UID. Use both columns to recover labels correctly. This ZIP is an output bundle, not an input accepted directly by the tree builder or ArrayPhyloViz. Extract the intended Newick and prepare array names/mapping for that specific tree.

docs.title: Editable figure data
docs.text: Use Save project in ArrayPhyloViz to produce crisprevo-composer version 1 JSON, then Open saved project to restore it. Do not manually change node IDs; annotations depend on them. The array-upload control also accepts supported crisprevo-spacermap version 1 metadata JSON and SVG files carrying supported SpacerMap/Composer metadata. Arbitrary JSON and image screenshots are not substitutes. Save private link stores an ArrayPhyloViz snapshot for seven-day recovery; Save project downloads the local reusable file.

docs.title: Limits and retention
docs.text:
These limits reflect the current code. A hosting proxy can impose stricter upload limits. An accepted job can wait in a queue before its analysis begins; a busy response without a Job ID requires a later resubmission.

Tool / area Limit SeqFetcher 500 unique IDs; 16,000 submitted ID-text characters; ID-list file up to 1 MB SeqFetcher requests At most 5 IDs per request; assembly-containing lists automatically use 1 SeqFetcher response 8 million residues per batch, including all contigs of an assembly SeqFetcher saved FASTA 25 million characters per job, including headers/newlines NCBI assembly package 64 MiB downloaded or expanded package size CRISPRPrep input 20 MB combined; up to 100 imported JSON files CRISPRPrep NCBI accession input 100 unique nucleotide/assembly IDs and 16,000 text characters; combined retrieved FASTA up to 20 MB CRISPRPrep extraction 100,000 arrays or extracted spacer rows CRISPRPrep minimum-spacer option Integer 1–10,000; default 2 CRISPR detection runtime 2 hours of detector processing; resource waiting can add elapsed time CRISPRPhylo runtime 15 minutes for inference; queue waiting is separate CRISPRPhylo repeat-distance option Nonnegative integer; default 0 SpacerTarget input 2 MB combined, up to 100 files SpacerTarget sequence format Each spacer 15–100 A/C/G/T bases SpacerTarget queries / occurrences 100 distinct sequences / 10,000 occurrences SpacerTarget search batches At most 10 distinct sequences and 1,000 bases per batch SpacerTarget target limit 20, 50 (default), or 100 targets per spacer SpacerTarget network Up to 200 displayed nodes; tables/exports retain all filtered rows SpacerTarget submitted search A batch exceeding 24 hours is marked failed ArrayPhyloViz Newick One tree, up to 1 MB ArrayPhyloViz tree 1,000 leaves, 4,000 nodes, depth 250 ArrayPhyloViz array text 4 MB ArrayPhyloViz arrays 1,500 arrays; 2,000 spacers per array; 20,000 total instances ArrayPhyloViz / CRISPRPhylo PNG 32 million pixels and at most 16,000 pixels per side SpacerMap raster DPI 36–2,400; default 300 My Jobs bulk link import 100 links/IDs per import Saved results and task records Seven days after the task ends

docs.title: What survives closing the page?
docs.text:
Once a Job ID appears, the accepted analysis continues on the server. Save its private link and retrieve it through My Jobs. The default browser history lasts only for the tab; Remember job history on this device preserves references locally but does not extend server retention.

Original input workspaces are deleted when a task ends. Saved outputs are not a complete archive of uploads, settings or logs. Keep those separately. Further ArrayPhyloViz edits need Save private link or a downloaded project; CRISPRPhylo rerooting changes only the current view/download, not the saved original tree.

For larger data, split analyses into biologically meaningful groups and use SVG for large figures. Download important results before expiry; opening a result link does not reset its expiry time.

docs.title: CRISPRPrep
docs.text: Use CRISPRPrep (/crispr-processing) to detect CRISPR arrays in genome sequences or prepare existing CRISPRCasFinder results. It produces a filtered spacer CSV for SpacerMap, CRISPRPhylo and SpacerTarget, plus a report explaining what was retained or excluded.

docs.title: Detect from sequence
docs.text:
1. Select Detect from sequence.
  2. Choose Upload FASTA and provide one .fa, .fasta or .fna, or choose Paste sequence and paste FASTA text.
  3. Include a unique > header for every contig and use IUPAC DNA letters. Do not paste a protein sequence or raw DNA without headers.
  4. Check detection-service availability. Refresh status checks it again.
  5. Configure processing below, then select Run.

One file can contain multiple contigs. Keep one biological sample per detection run: the tool does not automatically turn every FASTA record into a separate strain. For multiple strains, detect each separately, save each JSON, then import them together with distinct filenames or sample folders.

Detection requires an available server detector. If it is unavailable, use CRISPRCasFinder results generated elsewhere and follow the JSON route. Detection can run for up to 2 hours, in addition to time spent waiting for resources. Once a Job ID appears, detection and processing continue after closing the page. Save Copy results link and return through My Jobs or Retrieve previous results. Results expire seven days after the task ends.

docs.title: Fetch from NCBI and detect automatically
docs.text:
1. Select Detect from sequence → NCBI accession.
  2. Paste up to 100 unique nucleotide accessions, nucleotide sequence UIDs, or assembly accessions (GCA_/GCF_). Separate IDs with newlines, spaces, commas or semicolons.
  3. Set the processing filters, select Run, and save the private results link.
  4. Follow retrieval, detection and processing progress. Successful records proceed even when some IDs fail.
  5. Review Accession IDs needing attention and the retrieval summary before interpreting the arrays.

For example, GCF_000339015.1 retrieves an assembly with its component contigs, whereas NC_000913.3 requests one nucleotide record. Assembly contig boundaries and accessions are preserved. Repeated component accessions are included once; this is accession deduplication, not sequence-similarity clustering. A single assembly can therefore produce more than one unique sequence in the summary.

Successful sequences are combined into one detector FASTA, within a 20 MB limit. This automated route produces one detection result and does not automatically create one strain per requested accession. For multi-strain inference, submit each sample separately, download its generated JSON, name it by sample, and import those JSONs together. If the task is partially finished, retry failed IDs in a separate submission; do not interpret missing retrievals as genomes without CRISPR arrays.

docs.title: Import JSON results
docs.text:
1. Select Import JSON results.
  2. Upload one or more CRISPRCasFinder JSON files, or select Choose a results folder containing sample subfolders and result.json files.
  3. To try the workflow without a detector, select Load example JSON.
  4. Configure the filters and select Run.

Each JSON file supplies a sample identity. When importing sample_A/result.json, the parent folder supplies Folder; for a standalone sample_A.json, the filename supplies it. Duplicate identities receive suffixes, but descriptive sample names are easier to audit. The same rule applies to generated JSON re-imported for a multi-strain analysis: use names that identify the source sample.

docs.title: Set processing options
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect and when to change it Minimum evidence level All evidence levels (1) Inclusive threshold: 3 keeps levels 3 and 4. Use a higher threshold to restrict the result to higher-evidence detector calls. At level 1, missing evidence values are also retained; thresholds 2–4 exclude them. Minimum spacers per array 2 Keeps arrays with at least this many Spacer regions. Increase to exclude shorter arrays; decrease to 1 if single-spacer arrays are relevant. Remove unknown orientation (ND) Checked Excludes unresolved direction after trying CRISPRDirection as a fallback. Unchecking retains unknown-direction arrays without inferring an orientation. Exclude organisms with N-containing spacers Checked Removes all extracted rows with the same organism name if any extracted spacer in that group contains N. It can affect multiple files in the batch.

Evidence levels are detector categories, not probabilities or a percentage confidence. These options filter detector results; they do not change the detector's search parameters.

The N filter is organism-wide, not limited to the single spacer, array or sample. Identical organism descriptions across files are grouped together; empty descriptions are also grouped together. If many otherwise usable arrays disappear, examine this filter and the report before concluding that those samples lack arrays. Other ambiguous DNA letters can still remain; SpacerTarget requires A/C/G/T only.

docs.title: Read the results
docs.text:
Start with the summary: input files and detected arrays describe what was inspected; retained arrays and processed spacer rows describe what remains after filtering. Extracted spacer rows have passed evidence and minimum-count filters; processed rows have additionally passed the chosen direction/N rules.

The array table has one row per detected array:

Column How to read it Sample / array Sample grouping and array name; use these to trace the record to your input. Duplicate array names are made unique across the batch. Organism Name taken from the sequence description, not a new taxonomic identification. Evidence CRISPRCasFinder evidence category, or missing if not provided. Direction Resolved +/-, or unresolved ND. Spacers Number of spacer regions reported for that array before final filtering. Processing result Retained or the applicable reason for exclusion.

Select Filtered out to investigate missing arrays. Typical reasons are Below evidence threshold, Unknown evidence, Too few spacers, Unknown orientation, and Organism contains N. An array may violate several rules; the displayed reason is not necessarily every possible reason. Zero retained arrays can be a valid filtering outcome, not a failed run.

Expand Preview processed spacer rows to inspect the first 200 rows. Original sequence and reverse complement are separate fields; blank reverse-complement cells for positive arrays are expected. Effective repeat is the orientation-appropriate repeat for that row. For negative arrays, processing reverses spacer row order within the array and adds reverse-complement sequence/repeat fields. It does not overwrite the original spacer sequence.

Search, status filters and pagination affect the preview only. Downloads include all rows from the applied settings. To change filtering, reselect your original JSON files, or download CRISPRCasFinder JSON from a detection result and import it again, set the options, and select Run. Saved results omit the original uploaded files and processing options. The current form values must not be assumed to describe a restored result; record your chosen settings separately.

docs.title: Choose downloads and next steps
docs.text:
Download Contents Next use CRISPRCasFinder JSON Generated result.json, available for detection jobs including accession-based detection. Download it for reprocessing or multi-sample import. Keep uploaded JSON separately; it is not retained as a saved job output. Unprocessed CSV Folder, Organism_Name, Seq_Name, Orientation, Spacer_Sequence, DR_Consensus. Inspect rows after evidence/count filtering. Processed CSV Extracted fields plus Reverse_Complement_Sequence, Reverse_Complement_DR, Effective_DR; applies direction/N rules. Input for SpacerMap and CRISPRPhylo; original spacer sequences also support SpacerTarget. Download processing report Counts, warnings, array outcomes and retrieval summary where applicable. Saved reports omit processing options. Explain exclusions; retain a separate settings record for reproducibility.

Select the CRISPRPhylo, SpacerMap or SpacerTarget link below the downloads to transfer the processed CSV into that tool in the same tab. Review the imported input, then submit it there; transfer does not start another analysis. If browser storage prevents transfer, download Processed CSV and upload it manually.

For tree building, confirm that Folder represents the intended strains. For array plotting, preserve unique Seq_Name values. See Input formats for their different roles.

docs.title: Limits and common problems
docs.text:
Up to 20 MB total input, 100 imported JSON files, and 100,000 parsed arrays or extracted spacer rows are accepted. Empty results still download as CSV with headers.

Symptom Action JSON rejected Supply a CRISPRCasFinder result containing Sequences, Crisprs and Regions, not a saved figure project or processing report. Many arrays unexpectedly excluded Review evidence, direction, count and organism-wide N filtering. Only one strain appears downstream Check that multiple genomes were not combined into a single sample; inspect Folder values. Refreshed job cannot be recovered Retrieve the full ID/private link in My Jobs. After seven-day expiry, rerun with your saved input.

docs.title: CRISPRPhylo
docs.text: Use CRISPRPhylo (/tree-builder) to infer strain relationships from CRISPR spacer data. You can also request separate array trees within repeat groups. The page displays the strain tree, supports interactive rooting, and exports Newick and tree images. Use ArrayPhyloViz to combine a chosen tree with arrays.

docs.title: Prepare a processed spacer CSV
docs.text:
Use Processed CSV from CRISPRPrep, either transferred through its CRISPRPhylo link or uploaded manually. Each row is one spacer; keep the order within each array. All seven columns must be present, even when some cells are empty:

Folder,Seq_Name,Orientation,Spacer_Sequence,DR_Consensus,Reverse_Complement_Sequence,Reverse_Complement_DR
Field Meaning / check Folder Strain ID. Use the same ID for all arrays from one strain and distinct IDs for different strains. Seq_Name Array ID, consistent across spacer rows from that array. Orientation For -, reverse or reversed, the input validation uses the reverse-complement spacer column. Spacer_Sequence Original spacer sequence; used for other orientations. DR_Consensus Array repeat sequence; preserve the detector-derived value. Reverse_Complement_Sequence Required usable spacer sequence for reverse rows. Blank values can make those rows unusable. Reverse_Complement_DR Reverse-complement repeat; CRISPRPrep supplies it for negative arrays.

At least two distinct nonempty strain IDs and two usable spacer rows are required. This minimum does not guarantee informative cross-strain evidence. In particular, CRISPRFormer cannot infer a strain tree if no repeat group contains arrays from two different strains. Numbered TXT, genome FASTA and an unprocessed CSV lacking required columns are not valid substitutes.

docs.title: Select the method and settings
docs.text:
Setting Default How to choose Tree Inference method GraphMSA GraphMSA builds a neighbor-joining strain tree using graph-based array comparisons. CRISPRFormer uses a pretrained model. Model profile (CRISPRFormer) High-variation data Choose Conservative data, High-variation data or Mixed data according to your study assumptions. These are different models, not confidence thresholds. Repeat grouping distance 0 A nonnegative integer edit-distance setting. See the method-specific behavior below before changing it. Also build array trees Unchecked Enable before submission to generate a ZIP of array trees as well as the strain tree.

Repeat grouping distance has different effects in the two current methods. In CRISPRFormer, 0 groups identical normalized repeats; a positive value allows repeat sequences within that edit distance of a group's representative to join it. One edit is an insertion, deletion or substitution; a value of 1 is not 1% divergence. Assignment uses the first qualifying group, so it is not a guarantee that every pair of repeats within a group is within the threshold.

In GraphMSA, repeat families remain grouped by their repeat sequence. Despite the shared control's name, its current value adjusts spacer sequence edit tolerance within those families; increasing it does not merge different repeat families. Keep 0 as a starting point and record both method and value. Do not assume identical numerical settings make the two methods equivalent.

If the model profile or tolerance is uncertain, compare the stability of important groupings across justified settings. Do not raise a threshold solely to obtain a desired grouping.

docs.title: Submit and recover a run
docs.text:
1. Select the method, repeat-distance value and optional model profile.
  2. Check Also build array trees if needed. It cannot be added to a completed result without a new run.
  3. Paste CSV or upload one file; use only one input method. Load example supplies trial data.
  4. Select Commit. After a run the same submit control may read Build tree.
  5. Wait for the Job ID, then save Copy results link. Processing continues after the tab closes.
  6. Return through My Jobs or Retrieve previous results to inspect and download the result.

The inference process has a 15-minute limit; queue waiting is separate. Results expire seven days after the task ends. Keep the original CSV and a settings record for reruns. The saved result report retains method/profile, repeat distance and counts, but not the submitted CSV or full run log. A blank Run log in a restored result does not by itself indicate failure.

docs.title: Read the strain tree
docs.text:
Leaves are strains. Check that leaf names correspond to the intended Folder values. The saved report's strain count and usable spacer-row count describe the validated input, not statistical support; spacer rows are occurrences rather than distinct spacer types. Check the actual leaves too, since the inference depends on available repeat-group evidence.

Branching shows inferred grouping. Vertical order is a drawing arrangement, so adjacent labels are not necessarily the closest pair. A CRISPR-based grouping alone does not establish transmission or a whole-genome relationship.

Lengths and rooting need separate interpretation. Numbers after colons in View Newick source are branch lengths. Positive supplied lengths guide horizontal distances in the drawing; otherwise the viewer uses topology spacing. Do not interpret the tree as elapsed time without independent calibration. The web workflow does not add a separate bootstrap-confidence assessment.

For example, ((strain_A:0.1,strain_B:0.1):0.2,strain_C:0.3); groups A and B together in that rooted representation. The numeric branch lengths are not support percentages.

Drag inside the viewer to pan and scroll to zoom. With the viewer focused, use + / - to zoom and Home to fit the complete tree. The initial tree is fitted automatically.

docs.title: Choose a root
docs.text:
Control Effect Midpoint root Places the root halfway along the longest leaf-to-leaf path. Requires known nonnegative lengths on every edge and at least one positive length. Root on branch Enters branch-selection mode. Click a branch at the desired position to place a root there. Keyboard activation of a focused branch selects its midpoint. Restore original root Returns to the original inferred tree supplied by the saved result.

Press Escape to leave branch-selection mode. Midpoint rooting can be unavailable for trees with missing, negative or all-zero branch lengths. Use branch rooting only when you have a justified interpretation, such as an appropriate outgroup; a chosen display root is not new evidence for ancestry.

Root changes update the displayed tree, Newick source and downloads in the current page. The saved job retains its original tree. Download the changed Newick before leaving if you need to preserve that root, and use that downloaded tree in ArrayPhyloViz. Downloading directly from My Jobs retrieves the original saved tree.

docs.title: Read optional array trees
docs.text:
When requested, Array trees reports the generated count and offers Download array trees (.zip). There are no individual array-tree previews on this page; the main preview remains the strain tree.

ZIP member How to use it group_*.nwk A tree of arrays within one repeat family/group. These leaves represent arrays, not one leaf per strain. index.csv Group identifier, array count, tree filename and status. skipped_single_array means the group contained only one array and has no tree. labels.csv Use both group_id and tree_label to recover the original array_uid and identify strain/array membership. Labels are unique within a group, not necessarily across all groups. README.txt Description of the archive and its label mapping.

Array trees reuse the distances from the same analysis. Different files are separate within-group comparisons, not branches of one combined array tree. A count of zero can mean no group had enough arrays; inspect index.csv before treating it as an export failure. The ZIP is a separate download and is not embedded in the JSON report. It remains available from restored results until job expiry.

docs.title: Export and continue
docs.text:
Select Download .nwk for the currently displayed root. Choose SVG or PNG, then Download tree, for an image of the complete current tree independent of pan/zoom. PNG uses 2× rendering and is limited to 32 million pixels and 16,000 pixels per side; use SVG for larger trees.

Keep the input CSV, settings, original Newick, any rerooted Newick, and optional array-tree ZIP. Open ArrayPhyloViz, add the chosen Newick and corresponding SpacerMap TXT/SVG, and review mapping: tree leaves use strain Folder, whereas array names use Seq_Name. Multiple arrays may belong to one strain.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Action Missing columns or too few valid rows Use CRISPRPrep Processed CSV; check strain IDs and orientation-specific sequence fields. No cross-strain repeat group Check repeat sequences and sample grouping. For CRISPRFormer, reconsider repeat tolerance only if biologically justified. Missing code/model or no output tree Save the Job ID/error and contact the site administrator. Midpoint root disabled Inspect Newick lengths; missing, negative or all-zero lengths do not meet the requirements. A root change disappeared on reopening Expected: the job stores the original tree. Use the rerooted Newick you downloaded. Array-tree ZIP missing Confirm the option was enabled before submission; reopen interactive results rather than the generic report download.

docs.title: ArrayPhyloViz
docs.text: Use ArrayPhyloViz (/figure-composer) to align CRISPR arrays beside an existing tree, annotate the figure and export an editable project. It does not infer a new tree, reroot the tree or change branch lengths. Supply a tree from CRISPRPhylo or another analysis and arrays from SpacerMap.

docs.title: Load a tree and arrays
docs.text:
1. Under Phylogenetic tree, paste one Newick tree or upload .nwk, .newick, .tree or .txt.
  2. Under CRISPR arrays, paste numbered arrays or upload TXT/TSV, supported array JSON, or a newly exported SpacerMap SVG.
  3. Choose the name-matching rule, then select Commit. The tool composes the figure and attempts to save an initial private-link snapshot.
  4. Open Review & edit mapping before interpreting the figure.

For a first trial, select Load example, then Commit. This self-contained example uses matching strain names:

((strain_A:0.12,strain_B:0.08)95:0.05,strain_C:0.18);

strain_A    1,2,3,6,7,9
strain_B    1,2,4,6,8,9
strain_C    10,2,4,6,8

Newick requires unique leaf names and a final semicolon. Quoted labels are supported. Plain internal labels and branch lengths are retained; bracket comments are ignored. In this illustrative tree, 95 is an input internal label: ArrayPhyloViz displays it but does not calculate or validate its statistical meaning.

Use a SpacerMap SVG to preserve colors and source alignment positions. Use numbered TXT when only names, IDs and order are needed. PNG/JPEG screenshots and older SVGs without metadata cannot reconstruct editable arrays. CRISPRCasFinder JSON is not an array-figure project: convert it through CRISPRPrep and SpacerMap first.

To resume editing, select Open saved project and load the JSON produced by Save project. A supported ArrayPhyloViz SVG can also restore embedded project data when imported through the array upload control.

docs.title: Match arrays to tree leaves
docs.text:
Matching uses original Newick names, not row order or edited display labels.

Rule Example / behavior Exact names (default) strain_A matches leaf strain_A. Also strip _CRISPRn / _arrayn strain_A_CRISPR1 or strain_A_array2 can match strain_A. This is a specific suffix rule, not arbitrary substring matching. Ignore case and outer spaces Normalizes case and surrounding spaces; ambiguous normalized matches remain unassigned.

In Review & edit mapping, inspect each array's selected Tree leaf and Status. Choose the correct leaf manually when necessary. Search can narrow the mapping table. After changing the rule, Reapply name matching recomputes assignments, so recheck manual choices. Export the final correspondence with Export mapping TSV.

Several arrays can map to one strain; they form a group centered beside its leaf. Unassigned arrays remain in the project but are not drawn. Leaves with no mapped arrays remain visible. Neither an unassigned array nor an empty leaf proves biological absence: first check identifiers and mapping.

A common real-data mismatch is Folder versus Seq_Name: CRISPRPhylo names leaves from strain Folder, whereas SpacerMap names arrays from Seq_Name. Use the processed CSV to look up the correct strain for each array and assign it explicitly. Suffix matching only helps if your names actually follow that convention.

docs.title: Read the combined figure
docs.text:
Read each tree leaf together with its mapped array row or rows. Matching spacer IDs show shared types in the supplied numbering scheme. Numbered TXT from unrelated runs may reuse an ID for different sequences; prepare all arrays together in SpacerMap before combining them.

The tree depicts the relationships already present in the input Newick. Arrays display spacer type and order, not base-pair distances. Shared-spacer links help follow matching IDs; they are not evidence of transfer direction. Colors and row highlights are visual annotations you control, not automatically inferred biological categories.

Use branch lengths is off by default. Enable it when you want proportional horizontal tree distances. Scaling is used only if every edge has a nonnegative length and at least one is positive; check the note below the canvas for Branch-length scale or Topology scale. Turning it off changes the drawing, not the underlying tree.

docs.title: Adjust layout and inspect details
docs.text:
Drag empty canvas space to pan. Use + / −, Ctrl/Command plus wheel, or Fit to navigate. Find locates a leaf; Expand workspace enlarges the editing area. Screen zoom does not control export resolution.

Layout control Practical use Tree layout Choose rectangular or slanted branches without changing relationships. Array alignment Right/left aligns array ends; Source positions uses imported positions when available, such as a SpacerMap SVG. Tree width / Label space / Array width Increase the relevant region if branches, long labels or spacers are crowded. Row spacing / Label size / Branch weight Balance readability with figure size. Internal node labels / support Show labels already present in Newick; their meaning comes from the source analysis. Spacer IDs / Row guides / Export spacer legend / Shared-spacer links Include the visual aids needed by the reader. Filename name Set the figure's export name.

docs.title: Annotate a selection
docs.text:
1. Select a branch or node label and open Selection.
  2. Set Display label, branch/clade color, label color or clade row highlight.
  3. Select Apply annotation. Use Clear annotation to remove that styling.
  4. Use Rotate children to swap their display order, or Collapse clade to simplify a dense region. Expand all restores folded clades.

Display labels do not change matching IDs. Clade colors pass to descendants unless overridden individually. Collapsing hides detail in the view; it does not remove those descendants from the saved tree.

Select a spacer or legend item to edit fill/border colors and choose Apply to all occurrences. When an array is selected, Reverse displayed order flips its drawing only; it neither infers biological orientation nor changes source IDs. Use this deliberately and retain the project recording the edit. Undo and Redo help correct editing mistakes.

docs.title: Save an editable snapshot
docs.text:
After Commit, keep the private results link when saving succeeds. After changing mapping, annotations, layout or displayed array order, select Save private link again. Each save creates a new snapshot and Job ID; old links keep their earlier state. Reopen a snapshot with Retrieve previous results or My Jobs. Snapshots expire seven days after the save task ends.

If server saving fails, the current figure remains available. Download Save project JSON or retry Save private link. A downloaded project is the durable copy for later editing. Uploading/opening a local project does not by itself save subsequent edits to an existing server link.

docs.title: Save and export
docs.text:
Control Result What to use it for Save project ArrayPhyloViz JSON with tree, original IDs, mapping, settings, labels, colors, reversed arrays and collapsed clades. Resume editing with Open saved project. Save before closing or refreshing. SVG Vector figure with embedded editable project data. Further figure editing and supported re-import. PNG Complete raster figure at 1×, 2× (default) or 3×, independent of screen zoom. Slides and previews. Newick Full tree in edited child order with original names and lengths. Downstream tree tools; display labels/colors are not exported as tree annotations. PDF Direct PDF download sized to the complete figure. Share a figure without the browser print dialog. Most elements remain vector; non-ASCII labels are rendered as images to preserve their appearance. Use SVG/project JSON for editable text and project state. Export mapping TSV Array-to-leaf assignments. Audit sample matching alongside the figure.

Keep the project JSON, mapping and final figure together. An image alone does not preserve a separately readable mapping report or the original sequence evidence.

docs.title: Limits and troubleshooting
docs.text:
The editor accepts one Newick up to 1 MB, 1,000 leaves, 4,000 nodes and depth 250. Array text is limited to 4 MB, with up to 1,500 arrays, 2,000 spacers per array and 20,000 total spacer instances. PNG export is limited to 32 million pixels and 16,000 pixels on either side.

Symptom Action Arrays missing beside leaves Review unassigned rows and original names; map them manually. Labels overlap Increase label space or row spacing, or shorten display labels. Recoloring changes several rows Expected: spacer color applies to all occurrences of that ID. Branch lengths not reflected Enable Use branch lengths and check the layout note and input lengths. PNG too large Reduce scale or export SVG. PDF export fails Retry after refreshing the page and restoring your saved project; use SVG if PDF support could not load. Old SVG cannot be imported Use numbered TXT plus Newick, or a saved project JSON.

docs.title: SeqFetcher
docs.text: Use SeqFetcher (/ncbi-fetcher) to download nucleotide or protein records from NCBI by sequence accession, assembly accession or sequence UID. FASTA and metadata let you verify what was retrieved before continuing.

docs.title: Prepare identifiers
docs.text:
Paste IDs or upload UTF-8 .txt, .csv or .tsv containing IDs only, without a header. Separate IDs with newlines, commas, spaces or semicolons. Duplicate input IDs are removed.

NC_012920.1
NM_000546.6
NM_001126112.3

These are nucleotide retrieval examples, not a bacterial CRISPR dataset. Use sequence records corresponding to your study samples. A version suffix such as .1 identifies the requested record version.

Select Nucleotide for DNA/RNA or Protein for amino-acid records such as NP_000537.3. Numeric UIDs must belong to that database. For whole-genome assemblies, select Nucleotide and supply a GCA_ or GCF_ accession, for example GCF_000339015.1. Assembly IDs are not accepted in Protein mode. Gene, Taxonomy, BioProject and SRA IDs are not supported inputs.

docs.title: Retrieve sequences
docs.text:
1. Select the paste or upload input tab and enter IDs.
  2. Check the unique-ID count and any validation message.
  3. Select the database; keep nucleotide and protein requests in separate runs.
  4. Choose 5 · standard under IDs per request, or 1 · large sequences for large genomes. If the list contains an assembly accession, requests automatically use batch size 1.
  5. Select Commit and follow result statuses.
  6. Check organism, description and length against your sample list.

Stop after this batch requests cancellation; the active batch may finish and later IDs remain pending. Resume pending submits pending IDs as a new job. Retry failed submits all failed IDs as a new job, independently of row selection. The displayed result is replaced by the new job result; earlier successes remain accessible through the previous private link. Save that link before retrying or starting another run.

docs.title: Read results
docs.text:
Use the row statuses to follow retrieval. The downloaded run report records requested, succeeded, failed and pending counts; selected records can resolve to fewer distinct accessions.

Item Meaning Requested Unique input IDs in this run. Retrieved Input IDs resolved successfully. Failed IDs that could not be retrieved; inspect the error. Pending IDs not completed, for example after stopping or a service interruption. Unique sequences Distinct retrieved accessions. Different IDs can resolve to one accession, so this can be lower than the retrieved-record count. This is not similarity clustering. Length Nucleotide or amino-acid residues, depending on the database.

Search by ID, accession, organism or description, and use the status filter to locate unresolved records. A preview shows the FASTA header and first 2,000 characters; downloads contain the full sequence. For sequence-accession rows, View on NCBI opens the source record. For an assembly, use its GCA_/GCF_ accession to locate the corresponding NCBI assembly record.

Successful retrieval does not establish that the record is the intended strain, a complete genome or suitable CRISPR input. Verify metadata before analysis.

docs.title: Read an assembly result
docs.text:
An assembly appears as one accession row, but its FASTA can contain many chromosome/contig records. The reported length is the sum of their lengths. The downloader preserves separate FASTA headers and does not join contigs into one artificial sequence. Thus a count of one exported assembly is not necessarily one FASTA record.
